title: Chiller compressor vibration investigation procedure
chunkText: When a water-cooled centrifugal chiller reports rising compressor vibration together with a climbing leaving chilled-water temperature, first confirm the reading against the panel gauge, then inspect for refrigerant charge loss, fouled condenser tubes, and bearing wear. Trend the vibration against electrical input power; a simultaneous rise in both often indicates reduced heat-transfer efficiency rather than a purely mechanical fault.

steps: Verify leaving chilled-water temperature and vibration against local gauges.
Check condenser approach temperature and tube fouling.
Inspect compressor bearing oil analysis trend.
Compare electrical input power to rated load at current lift.
If degradation persists, schedule condenser tube cleaning.

title: Restoring chiller cooling capacity after performance loss
chunkText: Loss of cooling capacity on a centrifugal chiller is commonly traced to condenser water flow problems, non-condensable gases, or low refrigerant charge. Purge non-condensables, verify condenser water flow and tower approach, and confirm refrigerant subcooling. Document leaving water temperature before and after each corrective step.

steps: Run the automatic purge cycle and log non-condensable removal.
Confirm condenser water flow is within design range.
Measure subcooling and superheat; compare to commissioning values.
Re-test leaving chilled-water temperature under steady load.

title: Interpreting rising electrical input power on chillers
chunkText: A gradual increase in chiller electrical input power at a stable cooling load usually reflects a drop in coefficient of performance. Causes include condenser fouling, elevated condenser water temperature, or compressor wear. Cross-check kW against leaving water temperature and lift; do not treat instantaneous kW as accumulated energy.

title: 2024 plant-room chiller degradation episode
chunkText: Reduced cooling capacity accompanied by elevated compressor vibration and increased input power on the lead chiller. The unit drew noticeably more electricity while its chilled-water supply warmed over roughly an hour. Investigation found partial condenser tube fouling and a minor refrigerant undercharge. After tube cleaning and a charge top-up, leaving water temperature and vibration returned to baseline. No mechanical compressor failure was found.

history.symptoms: Reduced cooling capacity accompanied by elevated compressor vibration and increased input power.
history.investigation: Condenser approach temperature was high; tubes were partially fouled and refrigerant was slightly undercharged.
history.outcome: Condenser tubes cleaned and refrigerant topped up; performance recovered to baseline within two hours.

title: 2023 heatwave chiller efficiency complaint
chunkText: During a heatwave the chiller struggled to hold setpoint; occupants reported warm air while plant logs showed higher-than-usual power draw and creeping supply water temperature. Root cause was elevated condenser water temperature from a fouled cooling tower fill, not a chiller fault. Cleaning the tower restored capacity.

history.symptoms: Chiller could not hold setpoint during hot weather; higher power draw and warming supply water.
history.investigation: Cooling-tower fill was fouled, raising condenser water temperature.
history.outcome: Tower fill cleaned; chiller capacity and power returned to normal.

title: Chiller evaporator differential pressure monitoring
chunkText: Differential pressure across the evaporator reflects chilled-water flow. A rising differential pressure at constant pump speed can indicate restriction or strainer fouling. Add the differential-pressure point to the chiller only when a DP transmitter is installed; historical absence of this signal is expected and should be shown as unavailable, not zero.

title: Chilled-water pump low-flow troubleshooting
chunkText: If a primary chilled-water pump shows reduced flow rate, check the suction strainer, verify the VFD speed command, and inspect for a partially closed isolation valve. Cavitation noise with low flow suggests insufficient net positive suction head. Flow and head should track the pump curve.

steps: Inspect and clean the suction strainer.
Confirm VFD speed matches the control command.
Verify isolation valves are fully open.
Check for cavitation / NPSH margin.

title: Pump strainer blockage event
chunkText: The primary pump flow fell while motor current stayed flat. A blocked suction strainer was found and cleaned, restoring design flow. No bearing or seal damage.

history.symptoms: Falling flow rate at steady motor current.
history.investigation: Suction strainer was blocked with debris.
history.outcome: Strainer cleaned; flow restored to design.

title: AHU filter differential and supply air temperature checks
chunkText: Rising supply air temperature on an air handling unit with normal chilled-water supply may indicate a dirty coil, a stuck control valve, or an economizer fault. Check filter differential pressure and valve actuator stroke. Replace MERV filters per schedule.

steps: Read filter differential pressure and compare to clean baseline.
Verify chilled-water valve stroke and actuator feedback.
Inspect coil for fouling.
Confirm economizer dampers are commanded correctly.

title: AHU warm supply air due to stuck valve
chunkText: Supply air temperature drifted high while chilled water was available. The chilled-water control valve actuator was stuck partially closed. Replacing the actuator restored supply air temperature.

history.symptoms: High supply air temperature with chilled water available.
history.investigation: Chilled-water valve actuator stuck partially closed.
history.outcome: Actuator replaced; supply air temperature recovered.

title: Plant-room door-held-open handling
chunkText: A plant-room door-held-open event is logged when a door contact stays open beyond the configured threshold. Operators should confirm whether maintenance access is in progress. A door event occurring near an equipment anomaly is contextual only and does not establish a cause.

title: Access panel denied-entry reason codes
chunkText: Access-denied events carry a synthetic reason code and reader identifier. Common codes: INVALID_CARD, SCHEDULE_LOCKOUT, ANTIPASSBACK. These records contain no personal identity, image, or video data.

title: Plant-room lockout/tagout general procedure
chunkText: Before any intrusive maintenance in the central plant room, apply lockout/tagout to the affected equipment, verify zero energy state, and record the permit. This procedure applies to chillers, pumps, and air handling units alike.

steps: Identify all energy sources for the asset.
Apply locks and tags; verify isolation.
Confirm zero-energy state before work.
Record the permit and notify the control room.

title: R-134a charge and subcooling reference
chunkText: For R-134a centrifugal machines, confirm subcooling against the commissioning record before adjusting charge. Low charge reduces cooling capacity and can raise compressor vibration as the machine hunts. Never add charge without a leak check.

title: Condenser tube cleaning schedule and method
chunkText: Condenser tube fouling raises condensing temperature, which reduces cooling capacity and increases electrical input power. Brush-clean tubes at the scheduled interval or when approach temperature exceeds the alarm threshold. Record approach temperature before and after cleaning.

steps: Isolate the condenser water circuit.
Brush-clean each tube and flush.
Re-measure condenser approach temperature.
Return to service and trend leaving water temperature.

title: Using rolling baselines for equipment trend alarms
chunkText: A rolling baseline compares a current reading against the recent average, excluding the newest samples so a gradual drift cannot hide in an adapting mean. Require a minimum sample count before alarming and a few consecutive breaches to suppress noise. Correlation with nearby events is context, not causation.
